title: Sum of prime divisors of neighbours
why: sopf-neighbour map; five cycles confirmed; f can reach ~1.5n so no potential function; Collatz-type global convergence.

title: Lopsided neighbour map
why: Fixed: starts n>=3 other than 8. Collatz-type global convergence.

title: The shift-6 prime map
why: Cycles {6},(8,9) confirmed; sexy-prime starts give 2n+6 growth; global convergence Collatz-hard.

title: Density of the basin of 22 ↔ 34
why: Existence and positivity of basin density for a P-type map is harder than convergence results; no tools.

title: Growth rate of square-sum Hamiltonian cycles
why: Bregman gives upper ~(1/2)N log N; matching lower bound for cycle counts in sparse arithmetic graph hard.

title: Prime-sum Hamiltonian cycle count
why: Same as existing 'Prime-sum Hamiltonian count'; also implies the open prime circle (Filz) conjecture.

title: Square-sum matchings count
why: Bregman upper bound easy; lower bound needs many matchings in irregular sqrt-degree graph; normalisation should be N log N.

title: Primes on circles centred at the origin
why: Max prime-pair representations of n as p^2+q^2; even unboundedness needs strong prime-in-binary-form results.

title: Thue–Morse of P(n) and P(n+1)
why: Two-point Thue-Morse correlation of P(n),P(n+1); Chowla-type shifted correlation beyond Mauduit-Rivat methods.

title: Two large factors and one small
why: Seven cycles confirmed incl. 3307 loop; mixed P/p map global convergence is Collatz-type.

title: The P(n)+P(n+2)+1 map
why: Five fates confirmed (12-cycle through 9); Collatz-type convergence.

title: Peak height of the 2n+3 map
why: Polynomial peak bound for P(2n+3)+P(n) orbits; already Collatz-hard style control of climbs.

title: Largest-factor subtraction game
why: State-dependent prime subtraction game; density and infinitude of P-positions like Prime Nim, open.

title: Undecidability of Prime Nim variants
why: Decidability of Grundy periodicity over polynomial families; even f(x)=x case unresolved; no foothold.

title: Spanning cube-sum paths
why: Weaker form of existing 'Cube-sum paths' (Hamiltonian path for every large N).

title: Sum-Euclid sequence
why: Induction: S+1=q*m with m<next prime q', so q repeats until m+k=q', then S+1=q*q'; every prime appears in order.

title: Random square-sum transpositions mixing
why: Cutoff for interchange-type walk on square-sum graph; cutoff for transposition walks on general sparse graphs open.

title: Prime matrices generate SL2(Z)
why: Prime matrices have positive entries, so their products do too; cannot produce -I or matrices with zero/negative entries.

title: Largest prime factor of Markov numbers
why: Known only for Markov pairs P(xy)->inf (Rend. Sem. Padova 2006); single-number version open, S-unit type.

title: Apollonian packing with prime curvatures
why: Needs curvatures p*m with m p-smooth for every large p; beyond Bourgain-Kontorovich density-one results.

title: No-three-in-line in the prime grid
why: Upper 2pi(N) trivial; random two-per-column choice with alteration, sieve bound on collinear prime triples gives order pi(N).

title: Consecutive largest factors both 3 mod 4
why: Joint residue distribution of P(n),P(n+1); even P(n)<P(n+1) density 1/2 only known logarithmically.
